criteria.text: malformed sig_b64 is ALWAYS a refusal (distinct path, never conflatable with validity); keyless-forgery killer test; malformed-but-valid-base64 case.
criteria.witness: inventory.py: decode_signature raises SignatureRefused on a base64 or length error; verify_signature raises on every refusal and RETURNS the signed digest, which cmd_check and run_report.signed_inventory compare to inventory_digest(entries) — validity is an affirmative value from the key, never the absence of a complaint. Tests: SignedInventory::test_a_keyless_forgery_with_a_malformed_sig_b64_is_refused (record derived from the document by a forger with no seed, sig_b64='not*base64!' → exit 1 'malformed', no 'signature verified'; function-level: SignatureRefused raised, and the honest case returns inventory_digest), ::test_a_well_formed_base64_that_is_not_a_signature_is_refused_as_malformed (b64('short') → exit 1 'malformed'); gate mirror SignedInventoryRequired::test_a_malformed_sig_b64_never_binds ('signature does not bind' + 'malformed'). M14 and M14b (decode failure returned as None, in decode_signature and in verify_signature) both KILLED — u-sig-2-r2-mutants.txt.

criteria.text: find/place scoped to the find_blocks ranges exactly; a match outside is REFUSED, not honoured; sign never touches prose; unsigned write restored to the frozen behaviour.
criteria.witness: inventory.py: find_signature computes find_blocks and accepts only start<idx<end; any other match raises InventoryError '… sits outside every inventory block — not an envelope; refused' (exit 2) before anything is rewritten, so sign/_place_signature cannot touch prose; cmd_write no longer calls find_signature on the no-key path — _stale_envelope() is advisory-only and swallows InventoryError, so `write` with no --key exits 0 and writes exactly the pre-#386 bytes. Tests: ::test_a_signature_line_in_prose_is_never_an_envelope (check no-pubkey 0; check --pubkey exit 2 'outside', not 'unsigned'; sign exit 2 and the document byte-identical), ::test_unsigned_write_ignores_the_envelope_and_writes_as_before (stdout == the pre-feature line, stderr empty, prose line intact), ::test_sign_places_the_envelope_inside_an_inventory_block (kills M13), ::test_a_valid_envelope_outside_every_block_is_refused_not_honoured (a real signature moved to line 1 → exit 2 'outside'); gate: SignedInventoryRequired::test_a_signature_line_in_the_report_prose_is_refused. M13 KILLED (17 RED), M16 (stray line ignored) KILLED. NOTE: the axis reports asked for 'ignored'; the frozen spec says REFUSED as a would-be forgery — the spec was followed.

intent.goal: Answer every Required from round 1 of U-SIG-2 (PR #490 review): the keyless-forgery class (G-1) first, then block-scoped envelope discovery/placement with the frozen unsigned write restored (G-2), the two structural refusals pinned by killer tests (G-3, G-4), and one implementation of the enforcement switch (G-5).
intent.non_goals: no envelope-format change (U-SIG-1's), no new dependency, no network, no other file, no PR action, no weakening of any existing refusal
intent.ruled_out: Changing the envelope format or the canonical bytes (U-SIG-1's; the fix is in validation only); ignoring a stray SIGNATURE_LINE in prose — the axes asked for 'ignored', the frozen spec says refused-as-forgery, and ignore would let a second copy of the line sit in a document unremarked; keeping verify_signature's None-means-valid channel with an extra guard (the conflation IS the defect, so the verdict became an affirmative digest and every refusal an exception); dropping the STALE advisory from unsigned write (kept, advisory-only, never a refusal, so the frozen exit code and bytes are restored without losing the round-1 pin); a shared pubkey parser in dispatch-sign.py next to _seed (fenced off by the spec — parse lives in enforcement_key, inventory.read_pubkey stays for the CLI).
intent.why: Round 1 demonstrated a keyless forgery one token away from green (M14): the record is derivable from the document, so the whole scheme rests on checkvalid plus the decode branch in front of it, and that branch shared its return channel with 'valid'. BOT-1 let sign rewrite prose and the gate read an envelope the parser never inspects. Both are the class of bug this repository exists to refuse: a claim graded on the wrong evidence.
